html:
SMTO-POL-0001 — Your permission rules blocked this action

GUID: 060721a0-196b-4a00-91a4-1dec5b358812
Slug: permission-denied
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • SMTO's own permission rules don't allow this action, so it was stopped before it ran. Changing file or folder permissions on the computer won't change this.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Permissions next to the message box and look for a Deny rule that covers this action. A Deny rule there blocks the action for this prompt, this conversation or everywhere.
  2. If you want to allow it, change that rule to Ask or Allow and save, then ask the Agent to do the action again. SMTO checks your current rules each time an action is about to run, and allowing it fails while a Deny rule still covers it.
  3. Otherwise, ask the Agent to do the work a different way that your rules allow. Sending the same request again will be blocked by the same rule.

What success looks like

  • The action runs, or the Agent finishes the Task in a way your rules allow.

If it still fails

  • If you can't change Permissions or your account isn't an administrator, send the Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change file permissions on the computer or switch off safety settings to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The permission authority (or an account installation restriction) returned deny for the pending invocation at execution preflight or dispatch, or a permission grant was rejected because the effective policy still denies the pending operation; nothing was dispatched.

What this means

  • SMTO’s permission policy does not allow this pending operation. The execution boundary rejects it before dispatch; a policy-edit check can also reject a change that still denies the pending operation. This is application authorization, distinct from filesystem permissions on the target computer.

Why this can happen

  • The policy evaluation for the pending operation returned deny.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the denied operation and scope with the configured permission policy. If the operation is not intended, change the request; if it is intended, the user responsible for that policy must explicitly choose the appropriate supported permission.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the effective permission policy (global, conversation and prompt scopes) for the capability and arguments in the denial's resource_policy_block, then either change the requested operation or deliberately edit the policy in Permissions (Settings › Security › Policy / Permissions or the composer). Retrying does not bypass policy, and operating-system file permissions are unrelated.
  • Adjust the requested operation, or explicitly change the configured permission policy if that is your intent. Retrying does not bypass policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended pending operation is allowed by the current policy before dispatch, or the request is changed to a permitted operation.

What not to do

  • Do not disable safeguards or change operating-system permissions to bypass this application denial.

Technical notes

  • The configured permission decision denies the pending invocation; it does not change outcomes of previously completed operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-FIL-0022 — The computer didn't let SMTO use this file
  • SMTO-POL-0003 — This command's folder is outside the allowed area
  • SMTO-FIL-0055 — SMTO can't save there because the drive is read-only
